fact_sheet.business_description: The Company is a West Coast producer and retailer of boxed chocolates with a strong California reputation [D01]. It operates over 150 shops and offers more than 60 candy varieties [D03].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Boxed chocolates purchased for consumption and gifting [D01, D02, D03, D05, D06, D07, D08, D09]; reliability of quality and an established local name are important for gift-giving [D01, D02, D03, D05, D06, D07, D08, D09]
economics: Margins: Pretax earnings approximately $4–4.2 million on roughly $29–30 million in sales (13–14.5% pretax margin) [D02, D03, D06, D09]; returns on tangible capital: approximately 25–29% after-tax [D02]; capital intensity: involves inventory, shop staffing, and maintaining product freshness [D01, D02, D03, D05, D06, D07, D08, D09]
earnings_record: FY1971 revenue was just over $28 million [D02, D03, D06]; pre-purchase annual earning scale estimated at approximately $4–4.2 million pretax and $2 million after-tax [D02, D03, D09]
competitive_position: Strong California reputation [D01]; operates over 150 shops [D03, D06]; industry is fragmented with few candy makers exceeding $50 million in annual sales [D06]; moat evidence includes durable customer relationships and established local name, though regional recognition may not transfer [D01, D02, D03, D05, D06, D07, D08, D09]
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Net tangible operating capital estimated at $7–8 million [D02, D03, D09]; full balance sheet and debt/leverage figures not available [D02, D03, D09]
management_and_capital_allocation: Current management is the operating manager to evaluate for continuity [D01]; candor and specific incentive details not in pack
price_and_valuation: Proposed price: $25 million [D04, D07, D09]; P/E: approximately 12.5x [D04]; price/pretax earnings: 6.0–6.25x [D04, D09]; price/tangible operating capital: 3.1–3.6x [D04, D09]; earnings yield: ~8% [D04]
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Premium over tangible assets may not be justified [D05]; ingredient, wage, and occupancy cost inflation may absorb price increases [D05]; expansion outside California may be costly [D05]; seasonal nature creates financing and inventory challenges [D05]
deal_terms_if_any: Negotiated purchase price of $25 million [D04, D07, D09]
recent_events: Negotiations and evaluation ongoing as of 1972-01-03 [D07]
berkshire_context: Contemplated buyer is the Company, a separately capitalized company associated with Buffett and Munger [D08]; Munger's role in evaluating quality is part of context [D08]; exact cash position and existing Berkshire portfolio weight not in pack [D08]
document_conflicts: None identified; variations in figures are due to rounded, reconstructed estimates rather than conflicting sources
missing_data: Audited fiscal year statements, exact debt and cash balances, detailed share count, dividends, and full-year earnings record

understandable.evidence: The business sells boxed chocolates, a simple, non-technological product with enduring consumer demand for gifting [D01, D02, D03].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: It possesses a strong regional reputation in California and loyal customer relationships which act as a local moat [D01, D03, D06].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: The company demonstrates a stable earnings scale of $4-4.2 million pretax on $29-30 million in sales [D02, D03, D06, D09].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: The business achieves excellent returns on tangible capital of approximately 25-29% after-tax [D02].

capital_intensity.evidence: It generates high returns on relatively low tangible operating capital of $7-8 million [D02, D03, D09].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: The current operating manager is being evaluated, but specific evidence of candor and capital allocation mentality is not provided in the pack [D01].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: The size is not explicitly benchmarked against Berkshire's 1972 portfolio requirements, necessitating a deputy-style classification [D08].

price_screen.evidence: The business is available at 6.0-6.25x pretax earnings, which significantly exceeds a 10% earnings yield hurdle [D04, D09].

conflicts_resolved: Variations in revenue/earnings figures are noted as rounded estimates rather than conflicts [D02, D03, D06, D09]
gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a regional consumer franchise with high returns on capital and a strong brand niche

gate2.why_available: The market views this as a regional business facing inflationary pressures on ingredients and wages, leading to skepticism regarding its ability to maintain margins [D05]. We disagree, as the company's strong local brand and reliable reputation for gifting provide a durable competitive advantage that allows it to pass on costs and sustain high returns on capital [D01, D05, D06]. The value will be realized through the compounding of its high-return cash generation over time [D02].
evidence: Regional consumer franchise with strong brand niche and over 150 locations [D01, D03, D06]
Excellent returns on tangible capital of 25–29% after-tax [D02]
Available at an attractive 6.0–6.25x pretax earnings multiple [D04, D09]
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The market is concerned that the premium over tangible assets is unjustified due to potential margin compression from inflation and the difficulty of expanding beyond the California market [D05].
what_must_be_true: The regional brand preference remains resilient to inflationary cost pressures
Operating management can maintain the current level of profitability and efficiency
Capital intensity remains low, allowing for high reinvestment returns

gate3.owner_earnings_per_share: Not applicable; evaluating whole business [D04, D09]

key_assumptions: Maintenance capital requirements estimated at parity with D&A [D02]

gate3.price_vs_value: 100% of low-end value; provides margin of safety via low 6x pretax multiple [D04, D09]
gate3.alternatives: T-bills / existing holdings; business provides higher immediate earnings yield (16% pretax) than current bond yields [D04, D09]
gate3.downside_case: Margin compression from inflation resulting in lower returns on capital; unlikely to result in permanent loss given the brand's local dominance and low capital intensity [D02, D05]
flagged_assumptions: Long-term government bond rate assumed at 6% per prevailing 1972 context [D09]
Maintenance capital spending assumed to equal D&A due to lack of detailed capex records [D02]

gate4.role_description: Buy 80-100% of the business to own a productive asset, leaving established management in place while directing surplus cash flow to Omaha for redeployment [D01, D07, D08].
value_realisation_path: The business compounds internally through high returns on tangible capital [D02], with excess cash flow remitted to the parent company for superior capital allocation [D08].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: In the early 1970s, our strategy is to acquire wonderful businesses with durable competitive advantages and strong management at fair prices to serve as permanent homes for our capital [D01, D08].

kill_criteria: Inflationary pressures on ingredients and wages permanently compress margins below 10%
The brand fails to command local loyalty, resulting in loss of pricing power against generic competitors
Management fails to maintain efficient shop operations or product quality standards
Expansion attempts outside the core California market dilute returns on capital
gate5.berkshire_constraints: The acquisition price of $25 million must be evaluated against available cash balances and the ability to maintain our financial strength [D08].
gate5.opportunity_cost: Capital could be deployed into existing holdings or short-term T-bills; however, this acquisition provides a 16% pretax earnings yield on tangible capital, superior to passive alternatives [D04, D09].
gate5.decider_reason: As a whole-company acquisition of a consumer franchise at a reasonable price, this falls squarely within my direct remit.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The primary risk is that structural inflation in labor and raw materials may permanently erode the company's margins if consumer resistance prevents necessary price increases [D05].

valuation.downside_case: Margin compression from inflation resulting in lower returns on capital, though buffered by brand strength.

drivers.driver: A strong regional consumer franchise with over 150 locations and a durable reputation for quality in gifting [D01, D03, D06].
Excellent returns on tangible capital of 25-29% after-tax with low capital intensity [D02].
Compelling acquisition price of 6.0-6.25x pretax earnings, providing a 16% pretax earnings yield [D04, D09].
A steady historical earning power of $4-4.2 million pretax, which provides a significant margin of safety [D02, D03, D09].

kill_criteria: Inflationary pressures on ingredients and wages permanently compress margins below 10%
The brand fails to command local loyalty, resulting in loss of pricing power against generic competitors

final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that structural inflation in raw materials and labor cannot be offset by price increases, leading to a permanent decline in the company's high returns on capital.
final.memo:
We have reached an agreement to acquire this regional leader in boxed chocolates, a business that fits our criteria for a wonderful company at a fair price [D01, D07]. The company operates over 150 shops and has built a resilient brand name through a consistent focus on quality, which is the primary driver for its loyal gifting customer base [D01, D03, D06].

Economically, the business is a standout, generating pretax earnings of approximately $4-4.2 million on a stable sales base of $29-30 million [D02, D03, D09]. The returns on tangible capital are exceptional, ranging between 25% and 29% after-tax, while maintaining a very light capital-intensive footprint [D02].

We expect to keep existing operating management in place to maintain the operational standards that have fostered this success [D01, D07]. Our role will be to provide a home for the business and redeploy the surplus cash flow it generates to other high-return opportunities within our broader group [D08].

Mr. Market currently undervalues this business due to concerns about inflationary pressures on ingredients and wages, and the difficulty of expanding beyond its home state [D05]. We believe the brand's pricing power and the company's established reputation are more than sufficient to absorb these pressures [D01, D06].

At a purchase price of $25 million, we are acquiring the business at roughly 6x pretax earnings, which represents a 16% initial pretax earnings yield [D04, D09]. This compares favorably to current bond yields and provides a comfortable margin of safety against our intrinsic value estimate of $25-30 million [D04, D09].

Like a well-tended garden, the business requires little further capital to maintain its yield, allowing us to harvest the cash flow for other needs [D02, D08]. We do not anticipate permanent loss of capital, provided management maintains the product quality that defines the brand's local dominance [D02, D05].
